claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 typically requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C.
Previously reported lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens remain vulnerable to oxidation.
Previously reported lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens remain vulnerable to liquid plating-metal corrosion.
Adding a minor concentration of elemental Si to ZrB2 powder can facilitate densification at reduced sintering temperatures.
Si-modified ZrB2 can be densified by SPS below 1700 °C.
Si segregates to ZrB2 grain boundaries during sintering.
Si segregation during sintering produces a thin, continuous SiO2 phase at ZrB2 grain boundaries.
Elemental Si acts as a liquid-phase sintering aid in ZrB2.
Liquid-phase action by Si lowers the densification barrier of ZrB2 at reduced temperatures.
During high-temperature service, segregated Si oxidizes preferentially to form a self-passivating silica layer.
The silica layer inhibits oxygen ingress and thereby improves oxidation resistance.
The silica layer reduces wettability and chemical attack by liquid plating metals.
Compared with undoped and prior lower-temperature specimens, Si-modified ZrB2 will have improved densification and a denser microstructure below 1700 °C.
Compared with the controls, Si-modified ZrB2 will exhibit lower oxidation weight gain.
Compared with the controls, Si-modified ZrB2 will exhibit less oxide-scale spallation.
Compared with the controls, Si-modified ZrB2 will have superior durability in liquid plating-metal baths.
The proposed improvements apply under sintering temperatures below 1700 °C and during high-temperature oxidation and liquid plating-metal exposure.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator states that SiO2 forms in situ at grain boundaries during sintering, whereas the mechanism states that segregated Si remains available and oxidizes during high-temperature service to form the protective silica layer. The timing and chemical state of the protective phase are inconsistent.
